ai.literal: Lover / with message / that came / to the dream / what / will I do / indeed / feast
ai.translation: What feast can I possibly offer to the dream that came bearing a message from my lover?
ai.modern: என் காதலரின் தூதுடன் வந்த கனவுக்கு நான் என்ன விருந்து செய்து உபசரிப்பேன்?
ai.explanation: The speaker, longing for her absent lover, is comforted by a dream that brings a message from him. Overwhelmed with gratitude, she personifies the dream as a welcome guest. She wonders aloud what kind of feast or hospitality ('விருந்து') she could possibly offer to adequately thank the dream. This highlights the deep solace she finds in her dreams during their painful separation.

ai.literal: Carp painted eyes I as beg if sleep to the united one survival truth I will proclaim indeed.
ai.translation: If my carp-like painted eyes would only sleep as I beg them to, I would proclaim the truth of my survival to my lover who united with me.
ai.modern: நான் இரந்து கேட்டும் உறங்காத என் கயல் போன்ற மை தீட்டிய கண்கள் உறங்கினால், என்னோடு கலந்த காதலருக்கு நான் இன்னும் உயிரோடு இருக்கும் உண்மையைச் சொல்வேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own sleepless eyes, which resemble carp fish painted with collyrium. She begs them to close and sleep so that she might see her lover in a dream. If her eyes would only grant her sleep, she could meet the lover who once united with her and proclaim the truth that she is still surviving despite the agony of separation. The particle 'மன்' adds a tone of longing and slight despair, as her eyes refuse to sleep, denying her even a dream of him.

ai.literal: In the waking state / those who do not grant / in the dream / because of seeing / exists / my / life.
ai.translation: My life survives only because I see in my dreams the one who grants me no favor in my waking hours.
ai.modern: நனவில் என் மீது அன்பு காட்டாதவரை நான் கனவில் காண்பதால்தான் என் உயிர் இன்னும் நிலைத்திருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker's lover is physically absent and thus unable to show affection in the waking world. However, the lover appears in her dreams, providing the emotional sustenance she needs. The contrast between 'நனவு' (waking) and 'கனவு' (dreaming) highlights that her survival depends entirely on the illusion of the dream. The word 'காண்டலின்' (because of seeing) emphasizes that this mere vision is what keeps her 'உயிர்' (life) from departing.

ai.literal: By dream arises pleasure, in waking state those who do not grant having sought for bringing.
ai.translation: Pleasure comes to me through dreams, for they seek out and bring the one who grants no favor in the waking state.
ai.modern: நனவில் வந்து அன்பு செய்யாதவரைத் தேடிக் கொண்டுவந்து தருவதால், கனவினால் எனக்கு இன்பம் உண்டாகிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker finds solace in her dreams because they accomplish what reality cannot. While her lover is absent and does not bestow his affection upon her in her waking hours, her dreams actively seek him out and bring him to her. Because dreams have the power to unite her with the one who is otherwise unreachable, they become the true source of her romantic pleasure.

ai.literal: in the waking state / that which was seen, too / right there / dream too / indeed / seen / at the very time / is sweet
ai.translation: What was seen in the waking state was sweet right then; the dream too is sweet at the very time it is seen.
ai.modern: நனவில் காதலர் தந்த இன்பம் அப்பொழுது இனிமையாக இருந்தது; அதுபோலவே கனவும் அதைக் காணும் பொழுது இனிமையாகவே இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker reflects on the nature of her experiences with her lover. She states that the joy she experienced in her waking state was sweet exactly when it happened. In the same way, the dream she has of him is sweet at the very moment she experiences it. The lengthened vowel in 'கண்டதூஉம்' (what was seen) adds a lingering emphasis to her memory of the waking experience, while avoiding complex joining rules by being treated as a single unit here. By equating the two, she validates the comfort she finds in her dreams.

ai.literal: Waking-state called one-thing is-not if, in-dream lover will-not-depart indeed.
ai.translation: If there were no such thing as the waking state, my lover would never depart from my dreams.
ai.modern: நனவு என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒரு நிலை மட்டும் இல்லாமல் இருந்தால், என் காதலர் கனவில் என்னை விட்டுப் பிரியமாட்டார்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses a deep longing to remain in her dream world where she is united with her lover. She states that if the waking state ('நனவு') did not exist, her lover would never leave her side in her dreams ('கனவினால்'). The waking reality is seen as an unwelcome interruption that tears them apart. The particle 'மன்' (maṉ) conveys a sense of wistful longing and certainty about what could have been.

ai.literal: In wakefulness not-granting cruel-person, in dream why us tormenting?
ai.translation: Why does the cruel man who grants no favors in my waking hours torment me in my dreams?
ai.modern: நனவில் வந்து அன்பு செய்யாத கொடியவர், கனவில் வந்து எங்களை ஏன் துன்புறுத்துகிறார்?
ai.explanation: The speaker questions the behavior of her lover, who is absent during her waking hours. She calls him a cruel person because he does not show her any grace or affection when she is awake. Yet, he appears in her dreams only to cause her distress by his fleeting presence. The contrast between wakefulness and dreams highlights her continuous suffering, as she finds no peace in either state.

words.gloss: he who is in the heart

ai.literal: Sleeping time, shoulder-upon-he having become; waking time, heart-in-he he becomes, swiftly.
ai.translation: When I sleep, he rests upon my shoulders; when I wake, he swiftly moves into my heart.
ai.modern: நான் தூங்கும்போது என் தோள் மேல் இருப்பவர், நான் விழிக்கும்போது விரைந்து என் நெஞ்சத்திற்குள் சென்று விடுகிறார்.
ai.explanation: The speaker describes the constant presence of her lover, whether she is asleep or awake. During her sleep, he appears in her dreams and embraces her shoulders. The moment she wakes up, he vanishes from her side but instantly takes residence in her heart as a memory. The words 'துஞ்சும் கால்' (when sleeping) and 'விழிக்கும் கால்' (when waking) contrast her two states, showing that her lover never truly leaves her.

words.gloss: those who do not show love (acc.)

ai.literal: In reality, those who do not show love, they will blame - in dreams, the lover, those who do not see.
ai.translation: Only those who do not see their lover in dreams will blame him for not showing love in reality.
ai.modern: கனவில் தம் காதலரைக் காணாதவர்கள் மட்டுமே, நனவில் வந்து அன்பு செய்யாத அவரை நொந்துகொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks of how dreams help her endure her lover's absence. She declares that only women who fail to see their lover in dreams will blame him for not showing love in the waking state. Since her dreams grant her the illusion of his presence and affection, she is spared from resenting his actual absence. The word 'நோவர்' (they will blame or suffer) emphasizes the bitterness of total separation, which she avoids through the comfort of her dreams.

ai.literal: In waking state us he abandoned they say; in dream they see not I wonder this town's people.
ai.translation: The people of this town say he has abandoned me in my waking hours. Do they not see him visiting me in my dreams?
ai.modern: அவர் என்னை நனவில் பிரிந்துவிட்டார் என்று இந்த ஊர் மக்கள் பழித்துச் சொல்கிறார்கள். ஆனால் அவர் என் கனவில் என்னுடன் இருப்பதை இவர்கள் காண்பதில்லையோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine responds to the local gossip that her lover has left her. The townspeople only see her waking reality, where she is alone and suffering. She wonders if they are blind to her dreams, where he is constantly present with her. The contrast between waking and dreaming highlights her rich inner life, which remains hidden from the judgmental eyes of the town.
